title: NASA Launches Powerful New Telescope to Study Cosmic Mysteries
subtitle: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope begins a long journey to uncover the secrets of dark energy and dark matter.

summary.en: NASA has successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. The telescope will travel one million miles to reach a special location in space called L2. It is designed to study mysterious forces like dark energy and dark matter. The project was named after Nancy Grace Roman, a famous astronomer who helped create the Hubble Space Telescope. Scientists hope this mission will help us understand how the universe grows and changes.
summary.zh: NASA 已成功從佛羅里達州發射南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼太空望遠鏡。該望遠鏡將航行一百萬英里，抵達太空中稱為 L2 的特殊位置。其設計目的是研究暗能量與暗物質等神秘力量。該計畫以曾協助打造哈伯太空望遠鏡的著名天文學家南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼命名。科學家期望這項任務能幫助我們理解宇宙如何成長與變化。

paragraphs.en: A new era of space exploration began on Sunday morning as NASA launched its latest space telescope. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 7:26 a.m. ET. It was carried into the sky by a powerful SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. This large spacecraft, which is about the size of a tour bus, is now on a long journey to its new home in space, located one million miles away from Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 太空探索的新紀元於週日上午展開，美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）發射了其最新的太空望遠鏡。南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼太空望遠鏡（Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope）於美東時間上午七點二十六分，從佛羅里達州的甘迺迪太空中心（Kennedy Space Center）升空。它由強大的太空探索科技公司（SpaceX）獵鷹重型火箭（Falcon Heavy）載運升空。這艘體積約如遊覽車般大小的大型太空船，目前正踏上前往距離地球一百萬英里外太空新家的漫長旅程。

paragraphs.en: NASA officials expressed great excitement following the successful launch. Jackie Townsend, the project manager for the telescope, described the event as a "glorious dawn launch" and noted that the spacecraft was placed exactly where it needed to be. Shortly after the launch, NASA administrator Jared Isaacman confirmed that the telescope had successfully opened its solar panels. He reported that the ground team was receiving data from the spacecraft and that all systems were working as expected.
paragraphs.zh: NASA 官員在發射成功後表達了極大的興奮。該望遠鏡的專案經理傑基·湯森（Jackie Townsend）將此事件形容為「輝煌的黎明發射」，並指出太空船已精準進入預定軌道。發射後不久，NASA 署長傑瑞德·艾薩克曼（Jared Isaacman）證實望遠鏡已成功展開太陽能板。他回報地面團隊正接收來自太空船的數據，且所有系統皆運作正常。

paragraphs.en: The telescope is named after Nancy Grace Roman, who was NASA’s first chief astronomer. She is often called the "Mother of Hubble" because she was a major supporter of the famous Hubble Space Telescope. The new observatory is designed to be very powerful. According to NPR News, it will have the same sharpness as the Hubble telescope, but it will be able to see a part of the sky that is at least 100 times larger. This will allow scientists to take pictures of huge areas of space at one time.
paragraphs.zh: 這座望遠鏡以 NASA 首位首席天文學家南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼（Nancy Grace Roman）的名字命名。她常被稱為「哈伯之母」，因為她是著名哈伯太空望遠鏡（Hubble Space Telescope）的主要推手。這座新天文台的設計功能強大。根據美國公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，它將具備與哈伯望遠鏡相同的清晰度，但觀測視野卻至少大上一百倍。這將使科學家能夠一次拍攝大面積的太空影像。

paragraphs.en: Interestingly, the telescope has a unique history. It was not originally built for scientific research. NPR News reports that the spacecraft was first designed to be a spy telescope for the National Reconnaissance Office before it was donated to NASA. Now, it has a new purpose: to help humans understand the deepest mysteries of the universe. The telescope will travel to a location called the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point, or L2. This is a special spot in space where the gravity of the Earth and the Sun work together. This helps the telescope stay in a steady position while using very little fuel. The James Webb Space Telescope also uses this location to get a clear view of the universe.
paragraphs.zh: 有趣的是，這座望遠鏡擁有獨特的歷史。它最初並非為了科學研究而建造。NPR 報導指出，這艘太空船最初是為國家偵察局（National Reconnaissance Office）設計的間諜望遠鏡，後來才捐贈給 NASA。如今，它有了新使命：協助人類理解宇宙最深奧的謎團。望遠鏡將前往被稱為第二拉格朗日點（L2）的位置。這是太空中一個特殊地點，地球與太陽的重力在此處相互作用，有助於望遠鏡在消耗極少燃料的情況下保持穩定位置。詹姆斯·韋伯太空望遠鏡（James Webb Space Telescope）也利用此位置來獲得清晰的宇宙視野。

paragraphs.en: Before the telescope can start its main work, it must complete a long trip. Jeremy Perkins, a scientist working on the mission, explained that it will take more than three months to reach its final destination. During this time, the team will check every part of the telescope to make sure it is working perfectly. They will perform many tests to ensure that the focus and the pointing of the telescope are correct. This process is like checking a car before a long drive to make sure everything is safe and ready to go.
paragraphs.zh: 在望遠鏡能開始主要工作前，必須完成一趟長途旅行。參與此任務的科學家傑瑞米·柏金斯（Jeremy Perkins）解釋，它需要超過三個月的時間才能抵達最終目的地。在此期間，團隊將檢查望遠鏡的每個零件，確保其運作完美。他們將執行多項測試，以確保望遠鏡的對焦與指向正確無誤。這個過程就像在長途駕駛前檢查車輛，確保一切安全且準備就緒。

paragraphs.en: Once it is fully operational, the telescope will begin a "ghost hunt" to learn more about dark matter and dark energy. Dark matter is an invisible substance that scientists believe holds galaxies together. By studying how gravity affects the path of light, the telescope will help researchers create a map of both normal and dark matter. This will give scientists a much better idea of what this mysterious substance actually is.
paragraphs.zh: 一旦完全投入運作，望遠鏡將展開一場「幽靈狩獵」，以深入了解暗物質與暗能量。暗物質是一種科學家認為能將星系凝聚在一起的隱形物質。透過研究重力如何影響光的路徑，望遠鏡將協助研究人員繪製出普通物質與暗物質的地圖。這將使科學家對這種神秘物質的本質有更深入的認識。

paragraphs.en: Additionally, the telescope will study dark energy. This is a strange force that scientists believe is causing the universe to expand, or grow larger, at a faster speed. To study this, astronomers will look for exploding stars known as Type Ia supernovas. These stars are often called "standard candles" because they shine with a predictable brightness. By counting and studying these supernovas, researchers hope to understand how dark energy influences the growth of the cosmos. The mission represents a major step forward in our understanding of the universe, and the scientific community is waiting eagerly for the data it will eventually send back to Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，望遠鏡也將研究暗能量。這是一種奇特的力，科學家認為它正導致宇宙以更快的速度膨脹或擴張。為了研究此現象，天文學家將尋找被稱為 Ia 型超新星的爆炸恆星。這些恆星常被稱為「標準燭光」，因為它們發出的亮度是可以預測的。透過計算並研究這些超新星，研究人員希望能理解暗能量如何影響宇宙的成長。這項任務代表我們對宇宙的理解邁出重大一步，科學界正引頸期盼它未來傳回地球的數據。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To take off or depart from the ground (specifically for a rocket or aircraft).
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於描述物體被舉起，這裡指火箭發射升空。文中：The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 7:26 a.m. ET.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The act of directing or aiming a telescope toward a specific object in space.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （望遠鏡的）指向、對準目標的動作。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（指著），這裡作名詞，指望遠鏡對準目標的精確度。文中：They will perform many tests to ensure that the focus and the pointing of the telescope are correct.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Objects in space with a known, predictable brightness used to measure distances.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 標準燭光（天文學術語，指亮度可預測的恆星，用來測量宇宙距離）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上是「標準蠟燭」，這裡指天文學中亮度恆定的天體。文中：These stars are often called "standard candles" because they shine with a predictable brightness.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will be positioned at the L2 point?

options.A: To be closer to the James Webb Space Telescope for collaborative repairs.
options.B: To maintain a stable position while consuming a minimal amount of fuel.
options.C: To allow the telescope to capture images that are 100 times sharper than Hubble.
options.D: To avoid the interference of light from the Earth and the Sun during observations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，L2 點是一個特殊位置，地球與太陽的引力在此處共同作用，能幫助望遠鏡保持穩定位置並節省燃料。選項 A 錯誤，文章僅提到 Webb 也使用該位置，未提及合作維修。選項 C 錯誤，文章提到的是視野範圍大 100 倍，而非清晰度。選項 D 雖為天文望遠鏡常見需求，但文中並未以此作為選擇 L2 的理由。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the development of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope?

options.A: It was originally built by NASA scientists who specialized in spy technology.
options.B: It was designed from the beginning to be a successor to the Hubble telescope.
options.C: Its current scientific mission was not the original intended use for the hardware.
options.D: It required significant structural changes to be converted from a spy tool to a research tool.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第四段，該望遠鏡最初是為國家偵察局（National Reconnaissance Office）設計的間諜望遠鏡，後來才捐贈給 NASA 用於科學研究，這顯示其原始用途與現在的科學任務完全不同。選項 A 錯誤，它是間諜機構設計的，非 NASA 科學家。選項 B 錯誤，它原為間諜用途。選項 D 雖合理，但文中並未提及「大幅結構變更」的細節，故無法推論。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'standard candles' refer to?

options.A: Objects in space that have a known and predictable level of brightness.
options.B: Tools used by scientists to measure the physical size of dark energy.
options.C: A specific type of equipment used to illuminate dark matter in space.
options.D: The light emitted by the telescope's solar panels during the mission.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文章第七段明確解釋 Type Ia 超新星被稱為「標準燭光」（standard candles），是因為它們以「可預測的亮度」（predictable brightness）發光。選項 B 錯誤，它們是用來研究暗能量的工具，而非測量其大小的物理量具。選項 C 錯誤，它們是自然天體而非人造設備。選項 D 錯誤，這與太陽能板無關。

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope mission?

options.A: To test whether a spy telescope can be effectively repurposed for civilian space exploration.
options.B: To replace the Hubble Space Telescope by providing higher resolution images of the deep universe.
options.C: To investigate the nature of dark matter and dark energy to better understand the universe.
options.D: To demonstrate the effectiveness of the SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket in launching large observatories.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第六、七段詳細說明該望遠鏡的任務是進行「幽靈狩獵」（ghost hunt），以深入研究暗物質與暗能量，這是該計畫的核心科學目標。選項 A 僅是背景故事的一部分。選項 B 錯誤，文章說清晰度與 Hubble 相當，並非取代它。選項 D 僅為發射過程的細節，並非整個任務的主旨。
